title: The European tech ecosystem has collapsed relative...
content:
The European tech ecosystem has collapsed relative to the United States and China.
The US has roughly 700 billion dollar startups worth $2.9 trillion combined while Europe has only 107 worth $333 billion. 
To put this in perspective, that's roughly 6 times more startups in the US  and the gap keeps widening.
Also, When you remove Stripe from Europe's numbers, a company that's technically American but has its headquarters in Dublin for tax reasons, Europe loses about 15 percent of its total startup value. 
That one company dependency shows Europe isn't building its own tech giants anymore.
So what went wrong? The first big problem is regulation. 
Europe created rules like GDPR and the Digital Markets Act to protect consumers and ensure fairness which sounds good in theory. 
But in practice, these regulations created so much complexity and uncertainty that entrepreneurs got scared to take risks. 
Meanwhile, the US. has a lighter regulatory touch that lets companies move fast and innovate without constantly worrying about breaking some rule. 
Even worse, Europe's market is completely fragmented startups have to deal with different laws, taxes, and regulations in 27 different countries. 
A startup in France can't easily expand to Germany or Spain without jumping through expensive legal hoops. 
The second problem is money and talent. 
European venture capitalists are way more cautious than American VCs. 
Silicon Valley investors will take massive bets on young founders with crazy ideas but European investors play it safer and fund fewer risky ventures. 
Also, Europe's best entrepreneurs and engineers constantly move to Silicon Valley because that's where they'll actually get rich. 
When successful European founders sell their companies, they move to the US  to start their next one. 
It's a constant loss of experienced people who could mentor and fund the next generation. 
The real implication is that Europe is losing the technology race at exactly the wrong time. 
AI, semiconductors, and space technology are becoming the economic engines of the world, and Europe isn't in that race. 
Without its own tech companies, Europe becomes dependent on American and Chinese technology for everything.
What happened to the EU?
The US now has over 6 TIMES more startups than the EU with a combined value that is $2.2 trillion higher.
Even China is running laps on the EU, with more than double their startup value.
And, if you take Stripe out of the EU, which is only included for technical purposes due to their Dublin HQ, the EU loses ~15% of their total startup value.
Innovation in Europe is basically non-existent. 
- 
The Kobeissi Letter

title: Nancy Pelosi's portfolio returned about 950% from ...
content:
Nancy Pelosi's portfolio returned about 950% from 2012 to 2024, crushing both Warren Buffett's 445% return and the S&P 500's 439% gain. 
While her husband Paul executes the trades, the real story here is that members of Congress have access to nonpublic, market moving information that regular investors don't. 
They attend classified briefings, participate in closed door negotiations about legislation and vote on bills that can dramatically affect which companies profit or lose money. 
Research from Columbia University found that congressional leaders actually underperformed the market before gaining power, then suddenly started crushing it once they ascended to positions where they could access this privileged information. 
The pattern is consistent across both parties congressional leaders outperform regular members by up to 47% annually, and their stock sales are predictive of regulatory actions and hearings over the following year.​​
This creates a fundamental conflict of interest. 
How can you trust Congress to make decisions based on what's best for America when members are holding stocks that benefit from those same decisions? 
The system currently has almost no enforcement, the STOCK Act from 2012 imposed just a $200 fine for violations. 
This is why in September 2025, a bipartisan group introduced the Restore Trust in Congress Act to prohibit members, their spouses, and dependent children from trading individual stocks. 
Over 86% of voters from both parties support this ban, and it now has backing from both House Speaker Mike Johnson and Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. 
Removing the ability to trade stocks won't fix Congress, but it eliminates one clear, provable advantage that rewards insider access over actual competence or public service.
Nancy Pelosi absolutely DESTROYED Warren Buffett in the stock market since 2012.. 
This is insanity. https://t.co/obobX85C62
